cards.text: Jesus is still speaking when a Pharisee invites Him to dine with him. So Jesus goes in and reclines at the table. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer hoping somebody would invite me anywhere, so I'm already happy for Him.

cards.question: Jesus reclines at the Pharisee's table. What surprises the Pharisee?

answers.text: Jesus did not first wash before the meal
Jesus did not first give thanks for the meal
Jesus took the seat of honor at the meal

cards.text: Then the Lord says the Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish. Shiny lid on the cookie box, friend. Nobody's checking what's inside.

cards.question: When Jesus talks about the inside of the cup and dish, He's talking about what's inside the Pharisees.
Jesus says the Pharisees clean the outside. What does He say they're full of on the inside?

cards.text: Jesus doesn't tiptoe around it: "You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?" Then He tells them to give as alms the things that are within them.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees to give as alms the things within them. Then everything will be ___ for them.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Woe to you Pharisees!" They tithe mint, rue and every herb, counting out God's tenth the way I count sprinkles: one for the Lord, nine for the cookie, TWEEZERS OUT.

cards.question: The Pharisees tithe even their herbs, but Jesus says they disregard ___ and the love of God.
Jesus tells the Pharisees to stop tithing their herbs and practice justice instead.

cards.text: Woe number two: Jesus says the Pharisees love the greetings in the marketplaces. Walk through town, and EVERYBODY better say hi, or the whole day is ruined.

cards.question: Jesus says the Pharisees love greetings in the marketplaces. What does He say they love in the synagogues?

cards.text: Woe number three, and the picture gets strange. Jesus says they're like unmarked graves.

cards.question: Jesus says the Pharisees are like unmarked graves. What do people do with graves like that?

answers.text: Go the long way around them

cards.text: Jesus has been calling out the Pharisees at the dinner table, woe after woe. Then one of the experts in the law speaks up.

cards.question: Jesus is calling out the Pharisees when an expert in the law speaks up. What does he tell Jesus?

answers.text: Your words are true and wise

cards.text: Friend, the man basically raised his hand to get INCLUDED. And Jesus replies, "Woe to you as well, experts in the law!"

cards.question: Jesus says the experts in the law weigh men down with heavy burdens. What does He say they won't do?

answers.text: Lift a finger to lighten the load
Explain the reason for the rules
Pay the men who carry them

cards.text: That's the boss who drops a stack on your desk at 4:59 and walks out whistling. Next woe: the experts build tombs for the prophets.

cards.question: The experts in the law build tombs for the prophets, but Jesus says it was their ___ who killed them.
Jesus says that by building those tombs, the experts in the law are witnesses consenting to what their fathers did.

cards.text: Then Jesus says the wisdom of God spoke about sending them prophets and apostles.

cards.question: The wisdom of God says prophets and apostles will be sent to them. What does it say will happen to those prophets and apostles?

answers.text: Some will be killed and others persecuted
Some will be welcomed and others ignored
Some will be followed and others forgotten

cards.text: As a result, Jesus says, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets.

cards.question: Jesus says the blood charged to this generation goes all the way back to the foundation of the world.
Jesus names where that blood starts and ends: from the blood of ___ to the blood of Zechariah.

cards.text: From Abel, killed by his brother Cain (Genesis 4:8), all the way to Zechariah, killed between the altar and the sanctuary. And Jesus says, "Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation."

Last woe, to the experts in the law: Jesus says they've taken away the key to knowledge. The mystery key I shared a junk drawer with spent YEARS looking for its door, friend, and these guys just walked off with the key.

cards.question: Jesus says the experts in the law took away the key to knowledge and went in themselves.
The experts in the law took away the key to knowledge. What does Jesus say they did to those who were entering?

cards.text: Jesus goes on from there, and the scribes and Pharisees begin to oppose Him bitterly. Then the questions start, about many things, like a group chat that will NOT stop buzzing.

cards.question: The scribes and Pharisees ply Jesus with questions about many things. What are they waiting for?

answers.text: To catch Him in something He might say
To hear Him explain the Law to them
To hear Him take back all the woes

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-scene ('As Jesus was speaking'). The opening card says Jesus is 'still speaking' but never says to whom or what is going on, so the baker gets no context for the scene.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The Pharisees appear here for the first time, and the card never says simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The experts in the law appear here for the first time, and the card never says simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The scribes appear here for the first time, and the card never says simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The first sentence ('Jesus has been calling out the Pharisees at the dinner table, woe after woe') only recaps stop 1. It doesn't move the passage forward.

The joke blends the drawer key with the key to knowledge in one image. Its action (a key searching for its door) doesn't match the core action in the verse (taking the key away and blocking others), so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Zechariah, 'killed between the altar and the sanctuary,' is named without saying who he is. Which Zechariah is meant is debated (2 Chronicles 24:20-21 is often linked), and Luke doesn't say.
findings.question: The New people rule says to introduce someone the first time they show up, but Luke leaves this Zechariah's identity open. Should Papa Dorin identify him, for example as the Zechariah of 2 Chronicles 24:20-21, or leave him as only what Luke 11:51 says?
